tytul: Figs in balsamic vinegar: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for figs in balsamic vinegar: JarAtlas has no recipe for them from a checked source.

ostrzezenia.tekst: A boiling-water bath is suitable only for acid foods, such as fruits, pickles, jams and fruit butters, and only with the research-based process times of the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning.
Do not change the proportions of vinegar, food and water and do not use vinegar of unknown acidity; use only recipes with tested proportions.

For quick pickles, University of Wisconsin Extension advises: use only vinegar labelled 5% acidity; white and cider vinegar can be used interchangeably; do not use wine vinegars, homemade vinegar or lemon juice.

akapity: The FDA list gives Calamyrna figs a pH of about 5.05–5.98.
Figs have pH values slightly above 4.6, so figs canned as an acid food must first be acidified to a pH of 4.6 or lower.
White distilled vinegar and cider vinegar of 5% acidity are recommended for pickles.
Using a boiling-water bath for low-acid foods poses a real risk of botulism poisoning.
Without a tested recipe, there is no checked process time or vinegar proportion for figs in balsamic vinegar.
